$comment: kro-pwa's own nen declaration -- one lane (web), the pnpm/Turborepo monorepo TOOLCHAIN.md and the Makefile already name as the canonical entry points. Every verb below is that Makefile's leaf command, cited by file and line in its 'why'; nothing here invents a command the repo does not already run. Scenario react-uzf-v1 (Stack Matrix Scenario 5 -- Web Only), per CLAUDE.md.

dependency.name: nen
dependency.minimum_semantics: MAJOR.MINOR. At major zero a `0.A` pin is satisfied by an installed `0.B.z` when `A <= B` and either `A == B` or (`A` is at or above the binary's own compatibility floor and `B` is at or below the binary's own minor) -- nen decides this, and `nen shu tools --repo .` prints the exact range the verdict applied beside a `compat floor:` line naming the lowest `minimum` the installed nen satisfies; this prose is a convenience copy and nen's verdict wins. The floor moves only when a nen release's CHANGELOG carries a real breaking consumer bullet under `### Breaking / consumer notes`. v0.17.0 raised the floor from 0.7 to 0.17, v0.18.0 to 0.18, v0.19.0 to 0.19 and v0.20.0 to 0.20; this pin moved from 0.7 to 0.20 in one step on 2026-10-12, absorbing each release's consumer notes (gates `round_quorum`, `shu tools` exit 7 for a present-but-behind host, `wc catch-up` exit 3 on mechanical-only conflicts, `commit write` exit 3 on an injected trailer, the `classify` and `direct` verb families). A pin at or above the floor is satisfied by every later 0.x release that keeps it, so a repin is owed again when the floor moves and not when the minor does. Above major zero this reverts to the ordinary rule: `X.Y` means `>=X.Y.0 <(X+1).0.0`.
dependency.version_probe_output: a bare semver on stdout, e.g. '0.20.0' -- no 'v' prefix, no other text
dependency.$comment: What this repository needs FROM nen, as opposed to what nen runs IN it (`project`, below). `nen shu tools` synthesises a `nen` row from this block -- always verify-only, since re-pinning nen is `nen bootstrap`'s job and this repository's decision, never a side effect of a tools run. v0.20.0 is a PUBLISHED release carrying SHA256SUMS and the three platform binaries, which is what `bootstrap/nen.sh` verifies against; a tag with no release is refused at exit 6 by that script, so the pin is deliberately a released tag and not a branch or a bare tag. The pin matches zheref/hatsu's own nen/contract.json (the single source of truth for the dependency, D10) and zheref/KroApple's.

web.why: The workspace dependency install has run. Nen ASSERTS this and never performs it: 'make setup' / 'corepack enable && pnpm install' is the repo's own precondition (TOOLCHAIN.md 'First run'; Makefile 'setup').

build.why: Makefile 'build' -> 'pnpm turbo run build', fanning out to each workspace member's 'next build' (apps/web/package.json).

test.why: Makefile 'test' -> 'pnpm turbo run test', fanning out to 'vitest run --coverage' in apps/web and 'vitest run' in the two packages.

lint.why: Makefile 'lint' runs all three, in order: the repo-wide Biome pass, the per-workspace lint fan-out (which also runs @kro/core's platform-free check and @kro/app's UZF-boundary check), and the hanten review-round gate's own 40-case suite (make test-hanten-gate, scripts/test_hanten_gate.sh). Running only the second step is a weaker check than 'make lint' itself performs.

coverage.why: Makefile 'test-coverage', verbatim -- kept out of 'make test' and out of pr.yml on purpose (instrumentation roughly doubles the run; TOOLCHAIN.md). @kro/web's own 'test' script already runs 'vitest run --coverage' (apps/web/package.json), so the third step's lcov is real, not a gap. All three vitest configs declare 'reporter: ["text","lcov"]' with 'reportsDirectory: "coverage"' (packages/core/vitest.config.ts, packages/app/vitest.config.ts, apps/web/vitest.config.mts), so no reporter change was needed to name these paths. 'nen shu coverage' parses the first declared artifact whose format it recognises -- packages/core's lcov.info -- and reports the other two's existence without parsing them a second time.

ui-test.why: Makefile 'test-e2e', verbatim: the browser install is part of this verb, not a precondition, because the repo runs it every time (Playwright is not in pr.yml yet, TOOLCHAIN.md).

dev.why: Makefile 'dev' -> 'pnpm turbo run dev', fanning out to 'next dev' on :3000 (apps/web/package.json).

run.why: The production server (apps/web/package.json 'start' -> 'next start'). Requires a prior 'build': this repo has no Makefile verb for it at all -- the Makefile stops at 'dev'/'build' -- so nen states the production-serve invocation directly against the workspace member.

archive.unsupported: no packaging step exists for this lane. kro-pwa ships as a web application with no distributable artifact; the Makefile names no 'archive'-shaped verb and TOOLCHAIN.md documents none.

release.unsupported: Kro Web is a PWA -- there is no package or store pipeline. Makefile 'publish': "publish: n/a -- Kro Web is a PWA, there is no package or store pipeline. Releases ship via 'make deploy'."

deploy.unsupported: no target is wired yet -- host undecided, see TOOLCHAIN.md. Makefile 'deploy' is a stub that prints the open decision (Vercel vs Google Cloud Run) and exits 1 on purpose.

launch.$comment: project.launch is not read by nen 0.3.0 (preserved as an unknown key); the amaterasu skill reads it directly until 'nen shu dev --target' ships.

web.note: port precondition (3000, listening -> reuse) arrives with nen 0.4; until then the skill checks lsof by hand

evidence.$comment: Read by `nen shu evidence` and by hatsu:mukai step 7 / hatsu:shibari (UZF-26). MECHANISM CHANGED 2026-10-12 from files-changed to public-mirror: the maintainer asked for PR screenshots in the shape KroApple and KroAndroid use, so rendered-surface evidence is PNG captures recorded by Playwright from mock/stubbed data -- `apps/web/e2e/*-shots.spec.ts` writing under apps/web/e2e/__screenshots__/<suite>/<scene>.png, committed in git -- mirrored to the public zheref/kro-assets repository under kro-pwa/pr-<N>/ by scripts/pr_screenshots.sh and embedded through SHA-pinned raw URLs in the UZF-26 table. The landing-page effort's `apps/web/e2e/landing-shots.spec.ts` writes the first goldens there (19 scenes under __screenshots__/landing/, asserted with toHaveScreenshot); the older kc71-shots/kc79-shots specs write to an external KC71_SHOTS/KC79_SHOTS directory and record nothing here. A change that re-records no scene gets an empty row set from `nen shu evidence` (the truthful 'this change re-recorded nothing') and scripts/pr_screenshots.sh exits 0 with nothing to mirror; a UI change that records none declares the files-changed path of its RC-11 text snapshots under ## Evidence and names the gap. Only mock-fixture renders may ever be mirrored (the script confirms before pushing). Scenes are named {suite}-{scene} from the directory path (joined with '-') and file stem.
